rems.type: REMS with ETASU including prescriber certification, pharmacy certification, patient-provider agreement form, and patient wallet card to mitigate risk of suicidal ideation and behavior (SIB)
rems.detail: The SILIQ REMS Program is a restricted distribution program implemented to mitigate the risk of suicidal ideation and behavior observed in patients treated with brodalumab. ETASU elements include prescriber certification, patient enrollment via a signed Patient Enrollment Form, and pharmacy certification with dispensing limited only to authorized patients; distributors must also be authorized and may only supply certified prescribers and pharmacies. No specific laboratory monitoring is required under the REMS, but prescribers are expected to weigh risks/benefits and refer patients with new or worsening suicidal symptoms to a mental health professional.

boxed_warning.full_text:
WARNING: SUICIDAL IDEATION AND BEHAVIOR

• Suicidal ideation and behavior, including completed suicides, have occurred in patients treated with SILIQ.
• Prior to prescribing SILIQ, weigh the potential risks and benefits in patients with a history of depression and/or suicidal ideation or behavior.
• Patients with new or worsening suicidal ideation and behavior should be referred to a mental health professional, as appropriate.
• Advise patients and caregivers to seek medical attention for manifestations of suicidal ideation or behavior, new onset or worsening depression, anxiety, or other mood changes.
• Because of the observed suicidal behavior in subjects treated with SILIQ, SILIQ is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) called the SILIQ REMS Program.

key_safety: Key safety concerns include suicidal ideation and behavior (SIB rate 0.38 per 100 subject-years; 4 completed suicides in psoriasis trials; 6 total across all indications), neutropenia (grade 3/4 ANC decrease in ~0.4% of subjects), increased infections including candidiasis, and possible signal for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE rate 0.6 per 100 subject-years), though DCRP found no definitive causal link to MACE.
target_moa: Human monoclonal IgG2 antibody that binds interleukin-17 receptor A (IL-17RA), blocking biological activities of IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-17A/F heterodimer, IL-17C, and IL-25 (IL-17E)

_meta.indication: SILIQ is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy and have failed to respond or have lost response to other systemic therapies.

indication_details.prior_therapy_required: failed to respond or lost response to other systemic therapies

advisory_committee_detail.overall_recommendation: logic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC) on July 19, 2016, voted in favor of recommending approval (specific numerical vote not recorded in this document)

linkages.concern: Advisory Committee members expressed that brodalumab should be approved, that patient access should not be overly burdensome, and that providers and patients must be made aware of the suicidality signal. Committee members did not support withholding the drug from the market but rather advocated for meaningful risk communication and education as the appropriate risk mitigation approach.
linkages.change: The final approval structure was shaped directly by this AC message. Rather than requiring an additional randomized controlled trial (as some FDA reviewers had recommended) or denying approval, the agency approved brodalumab with a REMS with ETASU (including one-time prescriber and pharmacy certification plus a patient-prescriber agreement form), a Boxed Warning for suicidal ideation and behavior, and a restricted indication limited to patients who had failed other systemic therapies — all calibrated to be meaningful but not excessively burdensome to access.
linkages.evidence: "This approach to risk mitigation is consistent with the message heard clearly at the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC) meeting held on July 19, 2016, that this product should be approved, that access should not be overly burdensome and that providers and patients must be made aware of the suicidality signal."
